info.beegistics.bee_cell: An Applied Energistics 2 storage cell that holds Forestry bees. Each bee is stored as a compact genetic diff against its species' default, so a pure-species bee costs only a few bytes, a hybrid or mutated bee a few dozen, and identical bees collapse into a stack that is nearly free. There is no 63-type limit; a cell is bounded purely by its byte budget, so a cell full of closely related bees holds far more than one packed with wildly diverse genomes. Bees are stored as ordinary ME items and route through terminals, buses, and interfaces like anything else.

info.beegistics.bee_analyzer: A grid-connected block that analyzes bees anywhere on the ME network. Each tick it draws honey from the network's fluid storage into an internal buffer, then finds unanalyzed bees, analyzes them in place, and returns the analyzed bees to storage - so terminals and automation always see full genetics. Consumes honey and network energy per bee, mirroring the Analyzer it is built from.
info.beegistics.bee_requester: A grid-connected block that keeps a target bee stocked in the ME network by requesting real autocrafting jobs - it never breeds anything itself. Load it with a single Bee Pattern - a species with the pure traits you want - and set a maintain level. Whenever the network holds fewer than that, it submits a crafting job for the bee and hands the result back to storage. Because it only generates demand, it needs an Apiary Controller in Autocraft mode (or any provider of the pattern) on the same network to actually breed the tree.
info.beegistics.apiary_controller: A grid-connected block that automates Forestry breeding without bypassing its mutation chance or time. Place it against an apiary and load it with Bee Patterns - each authored as a species with the pure traits you want. It runs in one of two modes. In Standalone mode it is a simple perpetual breeder: it keeps each apiary stocked with a princess and drone matching a pattern and harvests everything back to the network, self-sustaining while replacements exist. In Autocraft mode it offers each pattern to the network's autocrafting system, so you can request the target in a crafting terminal and it schedules the whole breeding tree - and a Bee Requester can keep a target stocked for you. Place it against several apiaries and it drives all of them at once to breed in parallel. An apiary touching two controllers is contended and driven by neither, so the two never race over its workload.
